The agency's reading of the statute is entitled to deference. Under Chevron U.S.A. Inc. v. Natural
Resources Defense Council, Inc., 467 U.S. 837, 842-43 (1984), a court asks first whether Congress
has spoken to the precise question, and if not, whether the agency's answer is reasonable.
Courts apply the same framework to an agency's reading of its own jurisdiction. City of Arlington
v. FCC, 569 U.S. 290, 296 (2013). The Fifth Circuit has applied both steps to the Clean Water Act.
Southwestern Elec. Power Co. v. EPA, 920 F.3d 999, 1013 (5th Cir. 2019). So has the Eleventh
Circuit in the immigration context. Perez-Sanchez v. U.S. Att'y Gen., 935 F.3d 1148 (11th Cir. 2019).

[Respondent's reply] Chevron no longer governs. Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo,
603 U.S. 369 (2024).
